story.headline: Apple Introduces Refreshed iMac Powered by M6 Silicon and Dual 16-Core Neural Engine
story.summary: Apple officially announced the new 24-inch iMac powered by the M6 processor featuring core-integrated Neural Accelerators. The updated machine delivers up to 5x faster on-device AI performance compared to previous generations.

keyTakeaways: Apple refreshed the 24-inch iMac with the M6 processor, introducing a dual 16-core Neural Engine and on-core GPU Neural Accelerators.

According to Apple, on-device AI performance sees up to a 5x increase for local prompt processing over the previous M4 generation, with early Geekbench estimates pointing to around 40 percent faster CPU speeds.
Internal connectivity is upgraded with the Apple N1 wireless chip delivering Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, alongside optional 2.5Gb Ethernet.
Pre-orders open October 28, 2026, with retail availability beginning November 6, 2026, starting at an unchanged $1,499 base price.
draft.body:
On October 27, 2026, Apple announced an upgraded 24-inch M6 iMac, outfitting the desktop system with its latest silicon architecture and a dual 16-core Neural Engine. The hardware update retains the signature slim profile and seven-color palette of prior models while overhauling the machine's processing core to deliver up to five times faster on-device artificial intelligence performance compared to the preceding M4 model, according to [Apple's official product specifications](https://www.apple.com/imac/).

The introduction of the M6 chip brings dedicated Neural Accelerators inside each GPU core, higher memory bandwidth, and an expanded core count to Apple's all-in-one line. The computer arrives alongside an updated 14-inch MacBook Pro as part of Apple's late-October product releases.

[[FIG1]]

## Architecture Upgrades: Dual Neural Engines and GPU Acceleration

The centerpiece of the new desktop is the M6 system-on-chip, which Apple first deployed in the Mac mini in August 2026, as reported by [MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/27/apple-announces-new-imac-with-m6-chip-and-more/). Unlike previous generations that relied on a single neural processing array, the M6 integrates the first dual Neural Engine in the desktop line, featuring two 16-core engines.

Apple has also redesigned the graphics pipeline by embedding Neural Accelerators directly into each GPU core. Unified memory bandwidth expands to 170GB/s, up from 120GB/s in the M4 iteration. The base M6 silicon configuration supplies a 10-core CPU alongside a 10-core GPU, while an upgraded tier provides a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU.

Running macOS 27, the M6 iMac leverages this architecture for local processing within Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, as outlined by [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2298132/apples-imac-with-m6-arrives-promising-a-huge-leap-in-AI-performance/). The expanded neural hardware powers system-level capabilities such as Spotlight question synthesis, photo indexing, and contextual email retrieval without sending raw personal data to remote servers, utilizing Private Cloud Compute only when larger cloud models are required. Apple's official footnotes state that Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS, while Engadget notes that Apple Intelligence is not yet available in Europe.

[[FIG2]]

## Display, Connectivity, and Hardware Specifications

Externally, the desktop maintains the physical chassis established in earlier iterations, centered around a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display offering 500 nits of brightness and P3 wide color coverage, detailed on [Apple's iMac page](https://www.apple.com/imac/). Buyers can also select an optional nano-texture glass coating to mitigate reflections under harsh lighting conditions. A 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support remains embedded in the top bezel, paired with a studio-quality directional three-microphone array and a six-speaker sound system capable of Spatial Audio playback.

Wireless and wired connectivity receive significant technical revisions via the Apple-designed N1 chip, as reported by [9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/27/apple-launches-new-imac-with-powerful-m6-chip/). The N1 adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support, replacing the Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 standards found on the prior generation. Wired network transfers are accelerated through an available 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet port integrated into the power adapter, providing up to 2.5 times the throughput of the older Gigabit standard. Storage throughput is also up to twice as fast compared to the previous model due to PCIe 5.0 integration across internal solid-state drives.

Base models come equipped with two Thunderbolt 4 ports, while the 12-core configuration features four Thunderbolt 4 ports. Both configurations support driving up to two external 6K displays.

## Performance Benchmarks Across AI and Productivity

Apple reports noticeable performance differentials when comparing the M6 iMac against legacy platforms. In local AI workloads, the company cites up to a 5x increase in token prompt processing speeds within tools like LM Studio compared to the M4 iMac, and up to 12x the speed of the original M1 model, according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2298132/apples-imac-with-m6-arrives-promising-a-huge-leap-in-AI-performance/).

General compute benchmarks show equivalent gains. Based on early Geekbench results from the M6 Mac mini, CPU tasks are estimated to be up to around 40 percent faster than the M4 baseline, while Apple says graphics workflows see up to a 2x boost. In common productivity software, Apple states the system handles spreadsheets in Microsoft Excel up to 50 percent faster than the M4 desktop. When compared to the final Intel-based iMac, overall system speeds are rated up to 18x higher.

## Pricing, Configurations, and Availability

The 24-inch M6 iMac is scheduled to open for pre-orders on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at 10:10 a.m. Pacific Time, with official retail shipments commencing Friday, November 6, 2026, according to [MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/27/apple-announces-new-imac-with-m6-chip-and-more/).

The base configuration starts at $1,499, matching the price established earlier in the year. This baseline provides an M6 chip with a 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, the dual 16-core Neural Engine, 16GB of unified memory, 256GB of PCIe 5.0 storage, and two Thunderbolt 4 ports. The 2.5Gb Ethernet adapter is available on this model as a $30 upgrade. The $1,699 higher-tier configuration includes the 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, 16GB of unified memory, four Thunderbolt 4 ports, and the 2.5Gb Ethernet power adapter standard. Factory configurations scale up to 32GB of unified memory and 2TB of internal storage.

Each system includes a color-matched Magic Keyboard with Touch ID, Magic Mouse, power cord, 143W power adapter, and USB-C cable, available in green, yellow, orange, pink, purple, blue, and silver finishes.

faq.q: What is the starting price and release date for the M6 iMac?
faq.a: The M6 iMac starts at $1,499 in the United States. Pre-orders open October 28, 2026, at 10:10 a.m. PT, with in-store availability and customer deliveries starting November 6, 2026.

faq.q: What architectural changes did Apple make to the M6 chip in the iMac?
faq.a: The M6 incorporates a dual 16-core Neural Engine, dedicated Neural Accelerators inside each GPU core, up to 170GB/s unified memory bandwidth, and an expanded maximum layout of 12 CPU cores and 12 GPU cores.

faq.q: How does the M6 iMac compare to the previous M4 model?
faq.a: Apple reports that the M6 iMac delivers up to 5x faster on-device AI prompt processing, 2x faster graphics, and up to twice as fast SSD read and write speeds compared to the M4 model, while Geekbench benchmarks indicate up to around 40 percent faster CPU performance.

faq.q: What connectivity upgrades are included on the new iMac?
faq.a: Equipped with the Apple N1 chip, the computer supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. It also offers an optional or standard 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet port integrated into the external power brick.
